What do you do when you lose interest in just about everything?

Soldier on? Find something new to entertain yourself? Seek medical attention?
Folks of Voat, how do you deal when you just stop caring?
I try something new, that I've never tried before.

Sit down and start writing everything that comes to mind. Usually something interesting pops up.

Or, go find a nice place to sit, I prefer near a river, and just think. Figure out what your core values are. Figure out what you can do to move in the direction of those values.

Imagine you are 80 years old. What do you wish you had done? Do those things. Generally speaking, the longer time frame you consider, the better decisions you will make.

Another thing I like to do is figure out all of the different ways your identity is formed. In a lot of cases it's relational, so, for example, you are a son, a brother, a friend, a father, etc. List them all, then think of how you can be the best at each one, and then just start doing that.

Finally, if you're really stuck and nothing is helping, go talk to a professional. Most of them care a lot and do a great job helping people.

Its easy to get lost among the complications that plague our society, but what gets me motivated is that I have an obligation to all those in my family that came before me. The men and women that fought and survived and died just to make something for the next generation. Most of our hardships pale in comparison, and I owe it to myself, and to the people that came before me to enjoy the fuck out of everything they built for me. There are millions of things out there to do, try as many as you can. Don't make excuses for why you can't or don't want to do something, one of the most empowering things to do in life is attempting to achieve something you once thought impossible or unfavorable. You might feel you don't have a lot to care about, but you do, the simple fact that you exist right here and now is something to care a lot about, so invest in yourself and make yourself better today than you were yesterday, just like the thousands that came before you.
What's happened in the recent past that made you lose interest in everything?
Nothing. Life's good. Doing much better than a few years ago. Just feeling "meh."

Then it's similar to what I had gone through about a year or 2 back.

In short, it'll pass within a few weeks. You don't have to do anything about it really as otherwise you'd be forcing it. If you don't want to wait you can start a simple personal project where the final result is achievable within a day or 2. This way you can feel a sense of achievement which will generate more interest in other topics to bring your spirits up.
So far I just keep going because I know it's mainly just my situation that has me feeling this way.

I go outside and ride on a swing. I can do it for hours and just think about everything. Many interesting swingthoughts come to mind, just like showerthoughts in the shower. Especially it's great in the evening.

Sometimes it can be a sign of mild depression (dysthymia), especially if coupled with a loss of motivation and/or pleasure (anhedonia). If you think you fit into that category it may be worth seeking professional help, or at the least reading up on techniques to help you overcome it. I sometimes get that way when life becomes too easy and monotonous - try to switch it up a bit and set yourself a challenge (even if artificial).

I focus on bettering myself if I lose interest in everything else. I let myself lose interest a lot of things and feel meh from time to time, but when I come out of the meh phase, it makes the next phase that much better. Or you could do cocaine :-P

  2. If you aren't interested in anything, you might as well do something productive.
  3. It helped me to write down one good thing that happened every day and put it in a jar. It kept me focused on what was going on at specific moments and made my perspective more cheerful, since I was always looking for the "good thing" of the day.

  4. Things that help depression, and help it even better than pills long term:

     -eating healthily and regularly

 -sleeping enough, but not too much

 -spending at least half an hour outside in the sunshine every day

 -exercise (this one makes the biggest difference)
